author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read two Kaseya VSA 10 record types: notifications (alerts) and the audit log. A notification webhook posts alerts straight to HTTP Ingest, and bridges/kaseya-vsa10-audit-logs pulls the audit log from the API and posts each record there. Notifications go to the third-party alert schema and audit log records to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- Notifications (alerts) are pushed by a notification webhook created with POST /api/v3/notifications/webhooks, with Headers set to Authorization: Bearer <integration key> and the Url set to a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest integration.
- The audit log (script runs, remote control, file transfers, API token and account changes) is only available from GET /api/v3/auditlogs, so bridges/kaseya-vsa10-audit-logs pulls it and posts each record unchanged.

Field mapping:
- Notifications go to the third-party alert schema.
- The webhook body has a device identifier but no device name.
- Audit log records go to CloudAudit, with category and event type names from the API docs.

Made up in the samples:
- The audit samples follow the API's example record; the event descriptions other than its ad-hoc script example are made up, as are all values.

Testing:
- Both parsers passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 (83 of 83 fields matched the emulator).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- Pulseway's API docs describe the same webhook and audit log, so these parsers should read Pulseway too; that hasn't been tested.
- VSA 9.5 is a different product with a different API.
